title: cadintent rule registry artifacts
description: A rule registry is a versioned, content-hashed data artifact of rule entries — closed and no-eval: no entry ever contains executable code, and a conforming implementation ships a closed evaluator keyed by entry name. Released versions are immutable; changes are new versions, deprecated entries remain resolvable forever. The artifact's content hash is sha256 over its canonical bytes (the same canonical serialization as snapshots). Spec version 0.1.0.

Verification.description: The two-value verification marker on every rule entry. Only 'verified' entries can back a compliance pass; a check judged against an 'unverified' entry reports consistency with an unverified placeholder — a distinct, visible outcome that never reads as compliance.

RuleResult.description: What a rule entry's evaluation yields: the quantity kind and the quantum its value is quantized to (per the x-cadintent-quanta registry).

quantity.description: The quantity kind of the result, e.g. 'elevation', 'ratio'.

RuleProvenance.description: Who authored the entry and the basis citations it rests on — for taught rules, the engineer statement that birthed it. Basis is immutable; an entry's ancestry back to the engineer's words is permanent.

created_at.description: When the entry was authored (UTC, RFC 3339).

RuleEntry.description: One rule entry: a named, parameterized derivation — never executable code. 'params' is a JSON Schema for the parameter object (additionalProperties: false — unknown keys refuse); for check-parameter entries it doubles as the applicability predicate a check matches subjects against. Constant-valued entries (e.g. municipal minima) carry the quantized value in 'value'; a check that requires a value and finds none reports a finding, never a default.

params.description: JSON Schema for the rule's parameter object.

semantics.description: Normative human-readable description of the derivation.

value.description: The quantized constant value for constant-valued entries (e.g. a minimum slope). Absent for derivation rules whose values land in command payloads.

deprecated.description: Retirement marker set in a later registry version; deprecated entries always remain resolvable.

RegistryArtifact.description: One released registry version. Immutable: any change to any entry is a new version. A project brings a registry into scope with a registry.import declaration pinning id, version, and content hash; rule citations pin the exact imported version.
